stem:
Meera connects a small lamp to an electric cell using copper wires in her classroom. In which arrangement will the lamp glow?
A lamp glows only when there is a complete conducting path from one terminal of the cell, through the lamp, and back to the other terminal of the cell.

options.text: one wire connects one terminal of the cell to one side of the lamp, with no wire back to the cell
one wire joins one terminal of the cell to the lamp, and a second wire joins the other side of the lamp to the other terminal of the cell
two wires connect both sides of the lamp to the same terminal of the cell
the lamp is simply held touching one terminal of the cell with no wires

teacher.key_rationale: The lamp glows only when both terminals of the cell are connected to the two contacts of the lamp, forming a complete closed circuit (option B). Arrangements A, C and D leave the circuit incomplete or bypass the cell, so no current flows through the lamp.
